learning: Iteration 1 showed no oval oscillation problem at kp 1.6 and kd 0.5. Track this race's steering_oscillation on the oval against the 0.299 baseline, and slalom line_loss_events against the 1.0 baseline, to see whether the narrower track and wider span work together.
notes: Controller for the Builder's wider-span, narrower-track, lighter geometry. kp is scaled down by about 1/1.2 to offset the narrower track's higher yaw gain. base_speed and weights are unchanged from iteration 1 to isolate the geometry effect.
rationale: Iteration 1 (the only raced design, score 482.7) completed 20/20 oval runs at base_speed 1.0 with mean finish 1.69 s, so speed 1.0 leaves time margin on the 3 s limit. The s-bend finished 5/20 and the slalom 0/20, with every failure an off-track end where max_error reached 0.060 to 0.064 m while rms_error stayed at 0.023 to 0.030 m. The problem is peak excursion on bends. The Builder's geometry widens the span to +/-0.075 m (seven sensors at 0.025 m), moves sensors to y = 0.07 m, reduces wheel_track to 0.10 m and mass to 0.5 kg. Keeping the outer weights at +/-1.5 maps the same signal scale onto the wider span, so the weights stay as in iteration 1. Turn rate per unit of turn scales as 1/wheel_track, so the 0.12 to 0.10 m change raises yaw authority by about 1.2x. I lower kp from 1.6 to 1.4 so the effective position gain (about 1.68 against 1.6 in iteration 1) stays close to the tested value and oscillation does not rise. kd stays at 0.5, which iteration 1 used to damp the turn response, and the lighter mass gives a similar damping need. ki stays at 0.05 to avoid windup. base_speed stays at 1.0 so this race isolates the geometry change. last_direction line-loss recovery is kept because it re-enters the line on the side it was lost. Expected result, as a hypothesis: fewer slalom line-loss events and max_error below 0.06 m on the s-bend, with the risk of more steering oscillation from the narrower track.
